title: Stop the nightly reconciliation from flagging every payment

blocks.text: The payment service records each payment's time as an `Instant` taken from the system clock, and hands an audit library a copy made with `Date.from(...)`. Every night a job reads the copies back and lists the payments whose audit copy is missing or was edited. Since the service moved to a newer host, the job lists almost every payment, and nobody has touched the audit data.
`AuditReconciler.changed(...)` already walks the payments. Finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/AuditReconciler.java`:

items: `asStored(recorded)`: the time the audit library holds once it has been given `recorded`;
`matches(recorded, copy)`: whether the copy is still exactly what the library was given.

blocks.text: When you're done, an untouched copy never shows up in the list, and a copy that someone moved, even by a single millisecond, always does. About two lines in total.

cases.says: times with whole milliseconds, kept unchanged by the audit library, are not reported
a copy moved by seconds and a missing copy are reported, in the order of the recorded payments
a recorded time with microseconds whose copy the library kept unchanged is not reported
a recorded time in the second half of its millisecond whose copy the library kept unchanged is not reported
a copy that differs from the stored time by one millisecond is reported

origin.section: Date and Instant Name the Same Moment, but a Date Keeps Only Milliseconds

concepts: An Instant is compared with a Date at millisecond precision, truncating as Date.from does, never rounding and never with a tolerance.
Date.from(Instant) keeps only milliseconds, so an Instant with digits below the millisecond does not equal its round trip through a Date, while Timestamp.from keeps nanoseconds.
